target_definition.metric: United States high-yield corporate option-adjusted spread monthly change

graph_diagnosis.summary: Safe anchors connect business sentiment and issuance conditions to default-risk perceptions, investor demand, and high-yield market conditions.
weaknesses: A contaminated terminal node and its incident edges are excluded.

search_factors.why_search: Sentiment informs perceived issuer credit risk.
Issuance tests supply and market access.
Perceived default risk is a direct spread driver.

checkpoints.mechanism: Improving business sentiment reduces perceived issuer stress.
Healthy issuance supports market access and investor participation.
Sustained demand supports high-yield prices and tighter risk compensation.
Stable policy need not offset macro deterioration or supply pressure.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Policy, macro, and supply signals are compared.

checkpoints.factor: Default risk, demand, and supply balance
checkpoints.mechanism: Compare default-risk and investor-demand pressure against issuance, supply, and macro deterioration to infer spread direction.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Credit-risk, flows, issuance, and macro data reconcile.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Market conditions diverge from all underlying indicators.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: Improved credit perceptions and orderly issuance support investor demand and tighter risk compensation.
Macro deterioration or supply pressure can widen spreads despite stable policy.

alternative_hypotheses.discriminating_evidence: Compare issuance volumes, flows, and new-issue concessions.

forecast_audit_questions: Do sentiment and default-risk measures agree?
